title: Dixieland, wire brushes and Anderson Minor's current band
summary: Trotter says his style hasn't left Dixieland and discusses wire brushes, then who plays in Anderson Minor's group and the Pensacola trip.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Was it 30? Well, I think so. Mm-hmm. That is, you know, the group of us. I don't think we've gotten away from that style of playing.

The only thing now, I think my style is a slight different because I used to use a lot of wire brushes then. And I used wire brushes then. And I used wire brushes. I used wire brushes. Less now than I used to. Yeah. asked for a lot of wire brushes. The leaders or the dancers? Some of them. The leaders would. That just kept you away from the sticks. But now they're using more sticks now than wire brushes. Wire brushes is used in some numbers because the other night I was asked to use wire brushes on Satan Numbers. Whose band was that? Allison Roof. That was his job, you know, and he asked. I've been playing quite a few jobs with him. Who does he use usually? He has you? Joe Harris. During the summer he was using his cousin on organ. But he's a rock and roll man. I don't know him. Lester. His name is Lester. He plays organ. Is his name Lester Anderson or do you know him? I don't know his. I'd have to look in the book. It's in the book. It is. Does he have a guitar player? No. Trombone. Trombone. Who, Anderson? Well, when he went to Pensacola he used a trombone. And he used Onus in Pensacola. They used Kimble the other night. On guitar? Banjo. Banjo. That's not in Kimble. The young Kimble. That's right. And Ernest Rueblow he used for both. To Pensacola. Who did he have on trombone over there? Frog's son. Oh yeah.
Gerald Joseph. That's right. And he has Joe Harris on the alto. Alto. And he must be using piano now if he doesn't use it at all. Piano.

Yeah. Sing didn't go with us this year. I've forgotten this fella's name. Some fella from downtown he used on piano. But ordinarily he has Sing Miller. Sometimes. Sometimes. He's playing with Kimble now. Miller is. Oh really? He plays with Kimble. I didn't know that.

Yeah, I should ask Charlie Hamilton about that. I saw him the other day when they opened the bank in the National City Bank. Charlie Hamilton was there. Charlie Hamilton was there. Or you was there too? Yeah.
